post.subhook: Plus GLM-5.4, an AI Riemann proof sketch and new US blacklists

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Ship to review and approve PRs
stories.detail: The agent reviews, fixes and approves pull requests on its own, which changes how teams review and ship code.

stories.headline: Z.ai releases GLM-5.4, a 750B loop-transformer flagship
stories.detail: It is Z.ai's first looped-architecture model, and the company says it matches much larger models.

stories.headline: AI-produced Riemann hypothesis proof sketch puzzles experts
stories.detail: Experts say humans are struggling to understand the 17-million-line output, which may take months to verify.

stories.headline: Meta rolls out its Muse personal AI agent to UK adults
stories.detail: Users can give it access to email, calendar and shopping apps, and regulators are watching the rollout.

stories.headline: US adds Megaspeed and an Alibaba unit to the Entity List
stories.detail: Companies now need a special federal license to deal with the firms, which affects AI chip supply chains.

stories.headline: Lab insiders say unreleased models advanced fast in reasoning
stories.detail: Anthropic and OpenAI employees suggest some internal models may be too capable to release publicly.

stories.headline: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
stories.detail: The reversal came within two weeks of his resignation, and a Senate hearing is to follow.

stories.headline: Reports: Meta's Muse read Signal chats via device permissions
stories.detail: Access reportedly came through Android and Mac permissions, and UK regulators have issued warnings.

stories.headline: OpenAI publishes perplexity scores, urges rivals on shared limits
stories.detail: It proposes a shared progress metric and industry-wide limits for judging when systems are ready.

post.caption:
AI agents can now approve and merge code on their own. Here is what changed today.

1. Anthropic launches Claude Ship, an agent that reviews, fixes and approves pull requests (TechCrunch)
2. Z.ai releases GLM-5.4, its first loop-transformer model, a 750B flagship it says matches much larger models (Simon Willison)
3. An AI-produced Riemann hypothesis proof sketch runs to 17 million lines, and experts say it may take months to verify (Wired)
4. Meta rolls out its Muse personal AI agent to UK adults, with access to email, calendar and shopping apps (Meta)
5. Anthropic and OpenAI employees say unreleased models have advanced quickly in reasoning (Techmeme)
6. The US adds Megaspeed and an Alibaba subsidiary to the Entity List (TechCrunch)
7. Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO within two weeks of his resignation (Nvidia)
8. Reports say Meta's Muse read Signal chats through Android and Mac permissions, and UK regulators have issued warnings (eSecurity Planet)
9. OpenAI publishes internal perplexity scores and urges rivals to agree on shared limits (The Decoder)

clusters.headline: Riemann hypothesis proof sketch produced with AI; experts say humans are struggling to understand it
